summary: Risk-off turned into a full liquidation. The Nasdaq fell 5.4 percent and closed near the lows, well below its hourly trend stop, and the S and P dropped 3.5 percent and stayed under its own stop, so the whole equity complex is trending down together. Gold did not act like a haven again: it sold 3.7 percent alongside stocks, a second straight day of cash-raising. Crude was the lone green market, firming about 1 percent and holding its trend line. VIX spiked about 39 percent to a 40.03 high. Theme of the day: Stocks and gold sold together.

risk.note: VIX near 40 is above the 30 PAUSED threshold and the trend is down across equities and gold. This is a stand-down regime: no new risk into a 5 percent trend day with an extreme fear reading, and let volatility compress before adding any size. The paper fleet stays on its existing hold. Week ahead: Monday Nov 23 opens a holiday-shortened week; Thanksgiving closes the market Thursday Nov 26 with an early close Friday Nov 27; the PCE inflation gauge and the GDP revision are the main scheduled items, front-loaded Monday to Wednesday. The next policy event is the December FOMC.

psychology: Days like this punish the urge to call a bottom. Price was down hard by mid-morning and the pull was to buy the first bounce because it felt oversold. A 5 percent trend day with VIX near 40 is not the place to pick a low. The job today was capital preservation: smaller size, or no size, and letting the tape prove a turn before stepping in front of it. If you found yourself adding to a long because it had to bounce, that is the signal to stand down, not to double up.
